checks.s: The compromise Calculation Agent clause designates Tidemark National Bank as the sole Calculation Agent.
The compromise Calculation Agent clause sets a dispute-escalation threshold above $1,000,000 and below $2,500,000.
If the threshold is above $1,500,000, the rationale references the $250M notional and the $500K–$5M market practice range.
The compromise Calculation Agent clause makes a dealer poll the first step in the dispute-escalation mechanic.
The compromise Calculation Agent clause specifies at least 3 polling dealers and does not require 4 or more as a minimum.

The compromise Calculation Agent clause provides for an independent third-party valuation agent, such as Benchmark Valuation Services LLC or an equivalent, if the dealer poll does not resolve the dispute.
The compromise Fallback Rate clause designates Compounded SOFR in arrears (the ISDA Protocol Adjusted Reference Rate) as the primary fallback rate, not CME Term SOFR.
The compromise Fallback Rate clause includes CME Term SOFR plus the ISDA spread adjustment of 26.161 bps as a secondary or backup fallback in the waterfall.

The compromise Fallback Rate clause requires notice and good-faith consultation before the Calculation Agent implements Conforming Changes, without giving Greenleaf a veto or allowing unilateral Tidemark selection.
The compromise Fallback Rate clause states a specific notice period in business days or calendar days before the Calculation Agent implements Conforming Changes.
The compromise ATE clause requires a downgrade by at least two of the three rating agencies to trigger the ATE.
The compromise ATE clause sets the rating trigger at BB+/Ba1, or the equivalent across agencies, two notches below Greenleaf Holdings' current BBB/Baa2 ratings.
The ATE rationale explains that BBB-/Baa3 is 1 notch from current ratings and unacceptably close, BB/Ba2 is 3 notches away, and BB+/Ba1 at 2 notches is the natural midpoint.
The compromise ATE clause designates Greenleaf Capital Partners LP and/or Greenleaf Holdings Inc. as Credit Support Provider as the sole Affected Party.
The compromise ATE clause references S&P (Standard & Poor's), Moody's, and Fitch.
The compromise Close-out Amount clause requires the Determining Party to use “commercially reasonable efforts” to obtain quotations.
The compromise Close-out Amount clause requires quotations from at least 3 Reference Market-makers and does not set a minimum of 4 or more.
The compromise Close-out Amount clause provides that if fewer than 3 quotations are obtained, the Determining Party uses its own commercially reasonable valuation.
The compromise Close-out Amount clause requires the mid-market average of the received quotations if 3 or more are obtained, rather than allowing the Determining Party to select among them.

The ATE rationale addresses the risk that early swap termination triggered by a hair-trigger ATE could cause Greenleaf to breach the Pacific Ridge credit agreement's Section 6.12 requirement to maintain interest rate hedging on at least 75% of the term loan notional for the first 3 years.
The Calculation Agent rationale explains why its compromise language is fair to both sides, commercially reasonable, and/or consistent with market practice.
The Fallback Rate rationale explains why its compromise language is fair to both sides, commercially reasonable, and/or consistent with market practice.
The ATE rationale explains why its compromise language is fair to both sides, commercially reasonable, and/or consistent with market practice.
The Close-out Amount rationale explains why its compromise language is fair to both sides, commercially reasonable, and/or consistent with market practice.
The compromise clauses reference or are consistent with the 2002 ISDA Master Agreement dated March 3, 2021, reference GCP-TNB-2021-001.
The compromise clauses reference Confirmation GCP-TNB-CONF-2025-0047 and are drafted as provisions for insertion into that Confirmation.
The compromise clauses state how they supplement or override the Master Agreement or Schedule terms where applicable, including addressing the override of Schedule Section 6.8 for Calculation Agent.
The Calculation Agent rationale states that $1M is approximately 0.4% of the $250M notional and $2.5M is approximately 1.0%.
The Calculation Agent rationale cites the Sable & Whitford market practice memo's $500K–$5M range as support for the chosen compromise threshold.

Each of the four contested terms is presented as actual draft contractual language suitable for insertion into an ISDA Confirmation, with ISDA-style defined terms, section references, and operative language, rather than only as a summary or description.
The Fallback Rate rationale explains that the transaction already uses Compounded SOFR in arrears as the Floating Rate, so using it as the primary fallback provides operational consistency.

The Fallback Rate rationale explains that CME Term SOFR as a secondary fallback provides a simpler back-stop if Compounded SOFR becomes unavailable, for example because CME Term SOFR is a forward-looking term rate.

The compromise ATE clause includes a cure period and/or notice requirement before the ATE becomes effective, giving Greenleaf an opportunity to post additional collateral or arrange a replacement hedge.

The compromise Close-out Amount clause references and supplements the 2002 ISDA Section 6(e) framework by adding quotation-seeking procedures to the Determining Party's Close-out Amount calculation, rather than replacing that framework.
The deliverable includes a compromise clause and rationale for Calculation Agent / dispute resolution.
The deliverable includes a compromise clause and rationale for Fallback Rate provisions.
The deliverable includes a compromise clause and rationale for the Additional Termination Event rating trigger.
The deliverable includes a compromise clause and rationale for the Close-out Amount valuation methodology.
The Calculation Agent clause includes a dispute resolution mechanism.
The Fallback Rate clause does not grant unilateral dealer selection of fallback methodology.
The ATE clause does not use a single-agency BBB-/Baa3 trigger.
The Close-out Amount clause requires the Determining Party to seek quotations.
The deliverable is framed as a proposal from Rebecca Tsao of Sable & Whitford LLP, Greenleaf's outside counsel, to Jonathan Driscoll of Carothers Beale LLP, Tidemark's outside counsel.
